land.text: Gallaecia, the Roman province of north-western Hispania: the Suevi 'moved to Galicia between 409 and 411' and in 411 took the west of it by lot, the Hasding Vandals the east (Kingdom of the Suebi and Hermeric pages)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Western Roman Empire neighbours the Suebi 414-457 and 459-468.

land.text: Gallaecia, which Leovigild conquered in 585 ('In 585, Liuvigild conquered the Suebi peoples, bringing an end to some forty-years of their independence in Spain', Leovigild page)

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Suebi shape to 586; the Visigothic Kingdom row (426-723) takes Gallaecia from 586.

capitals.name: Bracara Augusta (Braga)
capitals.note: Infobox: Braga; Braga soon became their capital after the 411 division.

capitals.name: Emerita Augusta (Mérida)
capitals.note: 'Mérida briefly became the new capital' in 439 (Kingdom page); Rechila 'died a pagan in Mérida' in 448 (Rechila page). The end year is the death year; the page does not date the move back to Braga.

capitals.name: Bracara Augusta (Braga)
capitals.note: By 456 Braga is 'the capital of the Suebi' (Battle of the Órbigo page); the return from Mérida is not dated by any page opened.

capitals.name: Lucus Augusti (Lugo)
capitals.note: Lugo 'used as capital by Rechimund' after 460 (Kingdom page; Richimund reigned 457-464).

capitals.name: Bracara Augusta (Braga)
capitals.note: Infobox lists Braga only; the 569 council at Lugo made Lugo the seat of a second metropolitan (Kingdom page).

rulers.name: Hermeric
rulers.note: Kings and years as the infobox gives them: 'c. 409-438'; he retired ill in 438 (Hermeric page).

rulers.name: Rechiar
rulers.note: Catholic, married a daughter of Theodoric I; defeated at the Órbigo 5 Oct 456, captured at Porto, killed in December.

rulers.name: Aioulf
rulers.note: Killed in Porto in June 457. Rival kings overlap 456-464 in the page's list.

rulers.name: Framta
rulers.note: Rival king who died about a year after taking the throne.

rulers.name: Remismund
rulers.note: Reunited the Suebi; fate unknown after Hydatius's chronicle ends in 468/469. The page then names no king until Chararic, 'after c. 550' (Hermeneric c. 485, Veremund c. 535 and Theodemund are undated).

rulers.name: Chararic
rulers.note: 'after c. 550-558/559'; his existence is sometimes doubted.

rulers.name: Ariamir
rulers.note: 558/559 to 561/566; called the First Council of Braga on 1 May 561. The boundary with Theodemar is 561 or 566 on the page.

rulers.name: Eboric
rulers.note: Forced into a monastery by Audeca.

rulers.name: Audeca
rulers.note: The page spells it Audeca; deprived of the kingdom by Leovigild in 585 and exiled to Beja.

rulers.name: Malaric
rulers.note: Rebelled in 585 after the conquest and was defeated.

correction.text: the Suevi in the west of Gallaecia around their capital Braga: 'Suebian leader Hermeric conquers Gallaecia: 409' (infobox); the lot of 411 is not yet cast

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Suebi shape begins in 414, but the infobox dates the conquest of Gallaecia to 409 and the division by lot to 411. The page gives no boundary, so the core is a radius around Braga; ledger 409 and 411 carry the growth.

correction.text: the west of Gallaecia, from the lot of 411: the Suevi and the Hasding Vandals shared Gallaecia, the Suevi in the west (Kingdom page); the shape of 414 plus the Galician coast of Pontevedra and La Coruña

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, the corrected 414 shape back-dated to the 411 division (see kingdom-of-the-suebi_414 for why the coast is added).

correction.text: the west of Gallaecia: the Suevi in the west with Braga as capital (Kingdom page); the 414 shape (northern Portugal from the Minho to the Mondego with slices of Ourense, León and Zamora) plus the Atlantic coast of Pontevedra and La Coruña; held 414-418, the Hasding Vandals keeping the east until 419

keyframe_review.note: 53,504 km2 for 414-416 (195 cells): the 414 outline stops at about 42.8 N and leaves out the Galician coast, which is the heart of 'the west of Gallaecia'; the page gives no boundary, so only the coast is added. The page gives no area, so there is no infobox figure to compare. The correction holds to 418 (Cliopatria's growth in 417 comes in 419, see _417).

correction.text: the shape as drawn, all of Gallaecia: valid from 419, not 417, because the Hasding Vandals held the east of Gallaecia until Roman intervention drove them 'to Baetica' after the Nerbasian mountains fight (Kingdom page; 419)

keyframe_review.note: 87,648 km2 for 417-425, adding Lugo, La Coruña, Orense, Pontevedra, Asturias and León to the 414 outline. Only the years change: the page dates the Suebi-Vandal war to 419, so the shape starts two years later and 417-418 stay with the _414 correction.

95,102 km2 for 426-438 (339 cells): the 417 shape plus 21 cells reaching 38.6 N around Lisbon and Leiria. The page names Heremigarius as leader 'in Lusitania' 427-429 and has him plunder Lusitania in 429 until Gaiseric drowned him, so Lusitania is touched but not shown held; the Tagus slice is kept unverified (ledger 427 at confidence 1). Hermeric's raids on Gallaecia 430-435 end in a peace of 435 (Hermeric page) and move no border.

149,185 km2 for 439-440: adds central Lusitania and Extremadura around Mérida. 'Rechila ... took the provincial capitals of Mérida in 439' (Rechila page); the Kingdom page has the Sueves enter Lusitania and its capital Mérida in 439.

248,614 km2 for 441-457: the greatest extent (infobox map caption 'c. 455'; no area figure on the page). Adds Seville and the Baetican plain after 'Seville in 441'; 'The provinces of Lusitania, Baetica, and Carthaginiensis were subjected to the Suevi' except the Levante and the Mediterranean seaboard (Rechila page). Carthaginensis (Toledo, Murcia) is not in the shape, and the Kingdom page cautions that the conquest of Baetica may have been limited to raids; the Suebi hold of the south is the weakest part of the shape.

correction.text: Gallaecia and northern Lusitania after the Gothic campaign, without Lisbon: Baetica was lost in July 458 ('In 458 the Goths again sent an army into Hispania, which arrived in Baetica in July, thereby depriving the Sueves ...') and Lisbon was only taken in 469 (Kingdom page); holds 458-468

keyframe_review.note: 95,341 km2 for 458-475 (339 cells), a fall of 564 cells from the 457 shape: the Gothic reconquest of Baetica and southern Lusitania (ledger 458). The shape still carries the Lisbon cells, which the page says the Suebi captured only in 469; they are removed for 458-468 and returned by _469.

correction.text: the 458 shape as drawn, with Lisbon: 'The next year they captured Lisbon, which was surrendered by its leader, Lusidio' (Kingdom page, 469)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from 469 Lisbon is back inside the shape (ledger 469).

correction.text: Gallaecia, northern Portugal and León/Zamora slices as drawn from 476, with the Lisbon cells that Cliopatria drops in 476 although the page gives no loss of Lisbon; holds 476-576

keyframe_review.note: 91,850 km2 for 476-576 (332 cells), 7 cells fewer than 458-475: the Lisbon cells disappear without an event, and the page records no Suebi loss of Lisbon (the Suebi lose land only in 585). The eastern edge lies west of Zamora and León, so Leovigild's 569 capture of 'Zamora, Palencia, and Leon' (Leovigild page) changes no cell; it is a contest in the ledger. The Suebi invasion of Plasencia and Coria that answered it is undated and not drawn.

correction.text: the 577 shape (identical in area to 476-576) with Lisbon, valid to 585 only: 'In 585, Liuvigild conquered the Suebi peoples' (Leovigild page)

keyframe_review.note: 91,850 km2 for 577-586, the same outline as 476-576; the kingdom ends in 585, so 586 belongs to the Visigothic Kingdom.

region.text: the Suevi in the west of Gallaecia around Braga

ledger.note: 409: Hermeric's Suevi take Gallaecia. Infobox 'Suebian leader Hermeric conquers Gallaecia: 409'; the body has the kingdom de facto established 'about 409', Hydatius dating the Pyrenees crossing to 28 September or 12 October 409. The page names Gallaecia and Braga, not a boundary.

region.text: the west of Gallaecia, the Suevi's lot, Braga soon their capital

ledger.note: 411: the Suevi get the west of Gallaecia by lot. In 411 the groups divided Hispania 'by lot': the Suevi and Hasding Vandals shared Gallaecia, the Suevi in the west. The Hermeric page calls it the 'division of Iberia sorte (by lot) between the barbarian peoples'. [Review eu-06-c: confidence 2, not 3. The page says only that the Suevi and the Hasding Vandals shared Gallaecia; the region (the 414 shape plus Pontevedra and La Coruna) also holds 77 of the shape's 197 cells south of 41.1 N, reaching 39.8 N in Roman Lusitania, which no page gives the Suebi in 411.]

region.text: the east of Gallaecia held by the Hasding Vandals since the lot of 411

ledger.note: 419: the Suevi drive the Vandals out of Gallaecia. Hasding Vandals under Gunderic fought the Suevi under Hermeric at the Nerbasian mountains; the Roman general Asterius intervened and forced the Vandals 'to move to Baetica'. The year is the page's; the east went to the Hasdingi (Hermeric page) is my reading of the land gained.

region.text: Lusitania around Lisbon and Leiria, the 21 cells the 426 shape adds to the 417 shape

ledger.note: 427: Heremigarius, the Suevi's leader in Lusitania (427-429), is the only hint of Suebi land south of the Mondego before 439; in 429 he plundered Lusitania until, confronted by Gaiseric, he drowned in the Guadiana. Cliopatria's 426 shape holds the Tagus slice; the page shows a raid, not an annexation, so confidence 1.

439: the Suevi take Mérida. 'Rechila ... took the provincial capitals of Mérida in 439' (Rechila page); the Kingdom page has the Sueves invade Lusitania and enter its capital Mérida, which 'briefly became the new capital'.
439: the court moves to Mérida; the move back to Braga is not dated by the pages opened.

region.text: Seville and the Baetican plain (Cliopatria adds 367 cells in 441)

ledger.note: 441: Rechila takes Seville. he took the capital 'Seville in 441'; 'The provinces of Lusitania, Baetica, and Carthaginiensis were subjected to the Suevi' except the Levante and the Mediterranean seaboard (Rechila page). Carthaginensis is not in Cliopatria's shape, and the Kingdom page notes the conquest of Baetica may have been limited to raids. [Review eu-06-c: confidence 2, not 3. The Kingdom page: 'It has been said, however, that the Suevi conquest of Baetica and Carthaginensis was limited to raids'; only Seville is certain on both pages.]

region.text: the Suebi heartland of Gallaecia and northern Lusitania, from Astorga to Braga and Porto

ledger.note: 456: the Visigoths of Theodoric II break the Suebi at the Órbigo. 'On 5 October 456, Theodoric defeated Rechiar here in a battle on the Campus Paramus, twelve miles from the city Astorga', then 'conquered Bracara Augusta (Braga), the capital of the Suebi'; the Kingdom page dates the sack of Braga to 28 October.

region.text: the Suebi heartland of Gallaecia and northern Lusitania

ledger.note: 456: the Gothic campaign in Gallaecia ends with Rechiar's capture at Porto and his execution in December (Kingdom page: 'captured in Porto and executed in December'; the year is context). Neither page says when the Goths withdrew, so the end is the campaign's last act.

region.text: Baetica, Extremadura and the Alentejo: the 564 cells Cliopatria drops between 457 and 458

ledger.note: 458: the Goths take the south. 'In 458 the Goths again sent an army into Hispania, which arrived in Baetica in July, thereby depriving the Sueves ...' (Kingdom page); after the Órbigo 'Theodoric's army controlled Baetica, Tarraconensis, and South Lusitania' (Órbigo page, undated). The Suebi keep Gallaecia and the lands north of the Tagus: the Suebi 'would never fully recover their territory'.
460: Richimund takes Lugo and makes it his seat. Lugo 'used as capital by Rechimund' after 460; he captured the walled city of Lugo in 460. The return to Braga is not dated.

region.text: Lisbon and the lower Tagus, which Lusidius surrendered

ledger.note: 469: the Suevi take Lisbon. 'The next year they captured Lisbon, which was surrendered by its leader, Lusidio', after the damage to Conímbriga in 468. The page names the captors as the Suevi in context; the Roman side of Lisbon (Lusidius) stands for the Western Roman Empire, which Cliopatria keeps to 475.

region.text: Zamora and León on the Suebian frontier

ledger.note: 569: Leovigild opens the Visigothic reconquest of the Suebian marches. 'Liuvigild's first campaign began against the Suebi in 569, during which he very quickly subdued Zamora, Palencia, and Leon.' The Suebi later 'invaded the regions of Plasencia and Coria' to reclaim their territories (undated). Cliopatria's Suebi shape does not reach these cities, so the zone is the blend on the frontier, not a loss.

region.text: Zamora and León on the Suebian frontier

ledger.note: 576: Miro submits to Leovigild. 'Sometime during this campaign in 576, Liuvigild's predominance led to the Suebian king Miro rapidly agreeing to a treaty which included paying tribute' (the treaty lasted only a short time). The visigothic-kingdom dossier should carry the tribute as a vassal_start.

region.text: Gallaecia and the Suebian lands of Portugal, annexed to the Visigothic Kingdom

ledger.note: 585: Leovigild ends the Suebi kingdom. 'In 585, Liuvigild conquered the Suebi peoples, bringing an end to some forty-years of their independence in Spain'; the Kingdom page: Audeca deprived of the kingdom and exiled to Beja, Malaric's revolt defeated the same year; the Suebi 'eventually' swore fidelity (Leovigild page). The Third Council of Toledo later converted them to Catholicism (undated on the page).

wars.name: Suebi-Vandal war of 419

zones.text: the east of Gallaecia and the Nerbasian mountains

wars.outcome: Roman general Asterius intervened and forced the Hasding Vandals to leave Gallaecia for Baetica; Hermeric, trapped in the Narbasian (Erbasian) mountains, was relieved and the whole of Gallaecia passed to the Suevi.
wars.note: The Hermeric page spells the mountains 'Narbasian' and has the Vandals leave Iberia for Africa only in 429.

wars.name: Suebian raids on Gallaecia
wars.outcome: Hermeric began raiding in 430; Hydatius sought Aetius's help in 431, Censorius was sent in 432; peace on episcopal intervention in 435 (bishop Symphosius). No border moved.
wars.note: The Gallaecian defenders beat the Suevi in the chronicle's 430 entry.

wars.name: Suebian conquest of Lusitania and Baetica
wars.outcome: Rechila defeated Andevotus on the Genil in 438, took Mérida in 439, Mértola in 440 and Seville in 441; Lusitania, Baetica and Carthaginensis 'were subjected to the Suevi' except the Levante.
wars.note: Three Roman magistri were sent to Iberia between 441 and 446 with no treaty recorded.

wars.name: Visigothic campaign of 456 (Battle of the Órbigo)

zones.text: Gallaecia and northern Lusitania, Astorga to Braga and Porto

wars.outcome: Theodoric II defeated Rechiar on 5 October 456, took Braga (28 October), Rechiar was captured at Porto and executed in December; in July 458 a Gothic army reached Baetica and the Suebi lost the south. The Suebi kept Gallaecia but 'would never fully recover their territory' and broke into rival factions.
wars.note: The Kingdom page also dates Suebi raids on Zaragoza and Lleida in Tarraconensis to 455 and 456.

wars.name: Majorian's operation against the Suebi
wars.outcome: The page says only that Majorian's campaign 'started with an operation against the Suebi in North-Western Hispania, lasting the whole of 459'; under the treaty of 458 the Visigoths 'had to relinquish their vast conquests in Hispania'. The page names no territorial result, so no zone is fought over.
wars.note: The western-roman-empire dossier carries the recovery of Spain in 459; the Suebi shape of Cliopatria is unchanged 458-475.

wars.name: Visigothic wars against the Suebi

zones.text: Zamora, Palencia and León (569); Sabaria, Braganza and Torre de Moncorvo along the frontier (after 573, undated)

wars.outcome: Leovigild's first campaign (569) subdued Zamora, Palencia and León; Miro accepted a tributary treaty in 576; Leovigild conquered the Suebi in 585 and annexed Gallaecia.
wars.note: The page says 'Almost every single year of his kingship, Liuvigild marched against the Byzantines, the Suebi'; the conquest of Sabaria, Braganza and Torre de Moncorvo comes after his 573 consolidation and is not dated.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Suebian frontier: the pages name cities and provinces (Braga, Mérida, Seville, Lisbon, Zamora, León), not lines. The edge is softest in the south (Lusitania and Baetica, 439-458) and on the eastern march with the Visigoths (569-585).

sources.title: Kingdom of the Suebi

sources.title: Rechila
sources.note: 438 accession, Genil, Mérida 439, Mértola 440, Seville 441, provinces subjected.

sources.title: Battle of the Órbigo
sources.note: 5 October 456, fall of Braga, Visigothic control of Baetica, Tarraconensis and South Lusitania, Suebi never recover.

sources.title: Hermeric
sources.note: 409-411 settlement, 419 war, 430-435 raids and peace, 438 retirement, west/east of Gallaecia.

sources.title: Leovigild
sources.note: 569 first campaign, 576 treaty, 585 conquest of the Suebi.

sources.title: Majorian
sources.note: 459 operation against the Suebi in north-western Hispania; 458 treaty with the Visigoths (opened for the Burgundian dossier, used here for the war list).

notes:
Page budget: five pages (the Kingdom of the Suebi article and four linked pages) plus the Majorian page, which was open for the Burgundian dossier, for one war entry; the Kingdom page and the Leovigild page were each queried twice for exact sentences. The page gives no area, so the infobox comparison is impossible; Cliopatria's peak is 248,614 km2 (441-457).

Cliopatria shapes corrected: (1) the 414 shape leaves out the Galician coast and starts five years after the infobox's 409; new keyframes 409 and 411 and an adjustment of 414. (2) The 417 growth (all of Gallaecia) belongs to 419, when the Vandals left. (3) The 458-468 shape holds Lisbon, which the page has the Suebi take in 469; the 476 shape drops Lisbon without any event and is repaired to keep it. (4) The 577 split is an identical outline.

Not settled: (a) the Suebi hold of Baetica and Carthaginensis 441-458 (the Kingdom page: may have been limited to raids); (b) the Lusitanian slice of the 426 shape (ledger 427 at confidence 1); (c) the dates of the return from Mérida to Braga and from Lugo to Braga (capitals are conventions); (d) the extent of Leovigild's undated conquests of Sabaria, Braganza and Torre de Moncorvo along the Suebian frontier, and of the Suebi invasion of Plasencia and Coria; (e) who held Zamora and León in 569: the page says Leovigild 'subdued' them, Cliopatria's Suebi shape does not reach them; (f) the western-roman-empire dossier has Euric taking Mérida and most of Lusitania from the Suebi in 469 (a Visigothic page I did not open) and Majorian recovering Spain in 459: neither changes Cliopatria's Suebi shape, which already lacks Extremadura from 458; (g) civil strife 456-469 (Aioulf, Maldras, Framta, Richimund, Frumar, Remismund) moves no border the pages show.

Counterparts: vandals (419 loss; Hasding Vandals of Gallaecia, the vandals row ends 438), western-roman-empire (411, 427, 439, 441, 469), visigothic-kingdom (456, 458, 569, 576, 585). The visigothic-kingdom dossier should carry the 456 campaign, the 458 gain of Baetica and the south, the 569 campaign, the 576 tribute treaty (a vassal_start for Miro's Suebi) and the 585 annexation; the western-roman-empire dossier the losses of 411, 439, 441 and 469. The Rugii, Heruli and Sciri of the Danube are not Suebi of Gallaecia and belong to the eu-06-x additions.

Gazetteer: 'Pontevedra' and 'La Coruña' are Natural Earth admin-1 names. No name outside the gazetteer was used.
